summary: Create one PTY; command is sent once to its shell, or --agent starts a provider
usage: corral terminal create [--worktree VALUE] [--title VALUE] [--command VALUE] [--agent claude|codex|grok] [--model VALUE] [--effort VALUE] [--advisor VALUE] [--prompt VALUE] [--prompt-file VALUE] [--focus] [--request-id VALUE] [--help] [--json] [--timeout-ms VALUE] [--socket VALUE] [--instance VALUE]
examples: corral terminal create --worktree current --agent claude --model opus --effort high --prompt "review the diff" --timeout-ms 600000 --json
notes: Local macOS terminal backend guard v1 required (app/scripts/build-terminal-backend.sh); no automatic fallback to unguarded effects.
Handles bind profile, backend boot and PTY generation; runtime restart preserves handles when backend survives. Handles are not dispatch authorization.
Process conditions are unsupported and rejected without effects; general send targets current foreground.
Raw retention: last 1048576 bytes per PTY, backend lifetime; cursor is byte offset plus UTF-8 decoder carry. bytesBase64 is lossless; text is decoded UTF-8.
Read limit: 1..262144 bytes; screen limit: 1..262144 UTF-8 bytes; list limit: 1..10000. Input/command max 65536 UTF-8 bytes, title max 1024 bytes. NUL rejected.
Ready means transport, send means backend accepted, neither means application consumption or task completion. Close exitCode is null.

Request IDs: r1.<13-digit Unix milliseconds>.<UUID>, mint immediately before a new create/send; CLI mints if omitted. Retention 24 hours/10000 receipts; missing receipt for an admitted/older request or a pending receipt is unknown, never re-executed; lost results still count toward this runtime’s capacity.
Headless supports all commands except switch/focus and create --focus. Rename applies to every pane in the tab.

Agents (LIFE-394): terminal create --agent claude|codex|grok starts a managed provider in the new PTY. --model/--effort/--advisor/--prompt/--prompt-file require --agent; --command and --agent are mutually exclusive; --prompt and --prompt-file are mutually exclusive; --advisor applies to --agent claude only. Rejections are effect-free invalid_request.

Agent ready means two observations 750 ms apart that are all idle, interactive_ready and not launch-pending and that share one state_change_seq. wait --for agent-ready uses that gate; --for agent-idle applies the same gate to idle|done after a submission. A blocked screen returns satisfied false immediately instead of waiting for the deadline.

Prompt submission is fail-closed and effect-free when refused: detect_manifest_unverified when the guard's active detect manifest is not the expected bundled one, agent_blocked on a blocking screen, agent_not_ready when the ready gate or the compare-and-submit state_change_seq check fails, prompt_already_delivered when the provider record already holds the body.

A prompt without --wait is queued, not completed: herdr acknowledges the queue and corral has not seen the body in the provider record yet. --wait accepted confirms exactly one match inside the submission window (submit second floored, after the pre-submit cursor); --wait responded additionally needs an observed working turn and an assistant record after the match. Anything else is outcome unknown and is never re-submitted automatically.

create --prompt submits once at ready. If a blocker appears first the create ends there, complete, and does not hold the prompt — resume with terminal prompt under its own request id. The prompt stage of a create files its own receipt under the derived id r1.<create milliseconds>.<sha256("<create id>|prompt") first 16 bytes as a UUID>, and the receipt hash covers the body, so the same id with different content is request_conflict.

A prompt without --wait is queued, not completed: herdr acknowledges the queue and corral has not seen the body in the provider record yet. --wait accepted confirms exactly one match inside the submission window (submit second floored, after the pre-submit cursor); --wait responded additionally needs an observed working turn and an assistant record after the match. Anything else is outcome unknown and is never re-submitted automatically.

create --prompt submits once at ready. If a blocker appears first the create ends there, complete, and does not hold the prompt — resume with terminal prompt under its own request id. The prompt stage of a create files its own receipt under the derived id r1.<create milliseconds>.<sha256("<create id>|prompt") first 16 bytes as a UUID>, and the receipt hash covers the body, so the same id with different content is request_conflict.
